name: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.

peers.name: NVIDIA
peers.why: AI accelerator leader; direct rival to Instinct, same hyperscaler buyers

peers.name: Intel
peers.why: x86 rival in server and PC CPUs; Altera FPGAs vs Embedded

peers.name: Broadcom
peers.why: Custom AI chips for hyperscalers; competes for the same AI budget

peers.name: Marvell
peers.why: Custom AI chips and data-center networking; same buyers

peers.name: Qualcomm
peers.why: Snapdragon laptop chips vs Ryzen; entering data-center CPUs

peers.name: Lattice Semiconductor
peers.why: Pure-play FPGA rival to AMD Embedded (Xilinx)

valuation.vl3_basis: removed for AMD (Xilinx amortisation and 2023 losses make trailing P/E history meaningless)

dm4.name: Data Center revenue growth
dm4.source: AMD quarterly results release, segment table (on results)
dm4.what: Growth in AMD's Data Center revenue (EPYC server processors and Instinct AI chips) vs the same quarter last year.
dm4.why: Data Center was 58% of revenue in the Jun 2026 quarter (54% over the last 4 quarters) and nearly all of the growth story; the share price assumes AMD wins a real share of AI spending.
dm4.bull_means: Data Center is growing fast: AMD is winning AI and server business.
dm4.neutral_means: Data Center growth has slowed to a moderate pace.
dm4.bear_means: Data Center growth has slowed sharply: the AI story is not showing up in revenue.

dm4.name: Client revenue growth
dm4.source: AMD quarterly results release, segment table (on results)
dm4.what: Growth in AMD's PC processor (Ryzen) revenue vs the same quarter last year.
dm4.why: Client was 27% of revenue in the Jun 2026 quarter (29% over the last 4 quarters) and shows whether AMD is still taking PC share from Intel.
dm4.bull_means: PC chip sales are growing: AMD is gaining share.
dm4.neutral_means: PC chip sales are growing slowly.

dm5.name: Big-4 cloud capital spending growth
dm5.source: Quarterly results of Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta (capital expenditure); Platformonomics scoreboard
dm5.what: Combined capital spending of Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft and Meta in the latest quarter vs a year earlier.
dm5.why: These four are AMD's biggest Data Center buyers; their spending is the budget AMD's chips are bought from, and it is reported before AMD reports.
dm5.bull_means: The biggest buyers are still raising spending fast.
dm5.bear_means: The biggest buyers are slowing spending: less money for AI chips.

removed_indicators.reason: trailing P/E history is meaningless for AMD (losses in 2023 and Xilinx amortisation); removed from the score from 30 Sep 2026

chains.trigger: Taiwan tension or TSMC capacity limits

watch.name: news scan only
watch.active_if: any military, blockade or TSMC supply news

_settings_status: approved by Kenneth 30 Sep 2026 (DM4 Data Center 6 + Client 2; DM5 big-4 cloud capex; VL3 removed; VL4 kept; no overrides)

mix._note: Revenue mix (plan v0.4, not scored). Matched on the printed row label: AMD's 2022-24 filings attach the wrong member tag to some segment rows (e.g. Data Center tagged Client), so labels, not tags, decide. Client and Gaming profit is reported only combined from 2025 (2024 restated).
mix.note: Segment operating margin = the segment's operating profit ÷ its revenue, before company-wide costs AMD does not allocate (mainly amortisation of Xilinx purchase intangibles and share-based pay). AMD reports Client and Gaming profit only combined from 2025 (2024 restated the same way), so both show the combined margin.

_onboard_note: Price at the first staging build (29 Sep 2026 close): the reference for O6 winner discipline ("up since onboarded") until a positions feed exists.
